item.title: Re: "The Man of Nobody"
item.content:encoded: Before now I never actually read over SCP-3550, and that is indeed extremely similar. item.title: Re: "The Man of Nobody"
item.content:encoded:
Hello caspian2, thank you for responding! I appreciate the interest in the concept. After speaking in the IRC chat I discussed and most people said that due to the nature of this anomaly it would make sense if he developed it around 13~ when he went through his first breakup, however that wouldn't explain why the anomaly itself occured. I foolishly didn't preemptively think of how that'd be. I'll begin to brainstorm how to improve on the concept of how the anomaly was gained. I made a specific vow to not crosslink SCPs so I can't use another person's SCP, as I don't want to seem as if I'm riding off of their success - especially since this is my first SCP.

The reason they'd die the painful deaths is due to the curse/anomaly affected SCP-XXXX, which I still need to decide the cause of. I should be more specific and say that it's an extremely painful death - the pain dependent on how strong the mentioned relationship. Yes, acquaintance counts as a relationship. However it's only under verbal or written recognition where the effect appears. So if it simply isn't mentioned then it'll be fine.

With suicide patients, usually they can be sent to mental wards or the like to receive therapy. Inside of this therapy, usually catered towards people with extreme mental disorders, the main way which they're assisted by psychologists is via forming a strong, trusting relationship with them. However, he quite obviously can't do that.

I also decided during the time of discussion in the IRC chat that they actually turned themselves into the SCP foundation. I'd need to choose how they discovered the SCP Foundation, but that's the angle I want. They feel bad for wanting the attention so they try to trap themselves, but still get desperate and try to escape.

Due to Leveritas' advice, I've also decided to make a non-humanoid SCP first as that'd probably be a better way to start myself off. Thank you for the advice - I'll remember it for when I return to the concept later on in time.

item.title: Re: "The Man of Nobody"
item.content:encoded:
It's an interesting coincidence that you came to me about this, because I wrote SCP-3550, which is very similar in concept. Let me warn you beforehand, this is my most controversial skip because humanoids are just difficult to do well, expecially because you have to make them (or supporting cast) interesting characters in order for it to be enjoyable, which is easier said than done. Some people like it, others hate it.

I think your best angle will be to focus on how or why he was cursed, since I placed much more emphasis on the interaction with Foundation personnel and we might want to differentiate the two somewhat. That doesn't mean that you don't put effort into the Foundation personnel interaction also, maybe just shift your main focus on how your skip ended up in this situation.

Finally, making humanoids is incredibly difficult as a first one, so there's no shame in shelving it for now and revisiting the concept when you have more experience.

item.title: Re: "The Man of Nobody"
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Identity8866. Let’s take a look at your concept.

Overall, the concept was interesting at first, especially since you seem to be questioning the nature of human interactions and whether truly “No man is an island”.

Unfortunately, the concept falls apart rapidly due to plot inconsistencies or overcomplications that are not well explained. Why, for example, do people do when this happens? I believe it’s never explained / hinted at throughout your concept. Who placed this curse on him, and why?

Secondly, I don’t understand the nature of the anomaly. Okay, so they die “horrific” deaths, but how and why in those manners? You realise that a “horrific” death can be incredibly subjective, right? Some people would be terrified of dying alone, for example. More importantly, is there a reason why they die in such a manner?

Additionally, the concept itself is vague as “relationship” can mean pretty much anything? You mention “friend”, “enemy” and “loved one”, but isn’t an acquaintance also considered a relationship? Wouldn’t the Foundation agents who try and contain the man also be affected then?

Finally, I don’t understand that whole angle with suicide patients. How are they being “helped”?

Overall, there are too many plot issues for me to understand this fully. If you do decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. Best of luck!

item.title: "Man of None"
item.content:encoded:
Anyone who acknowledges a relationship between the man and themselves dies painfully within 24 hours.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes, however also seeking advice if possible.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror / Drama / Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): It'll begin as a standardized SCP document, listing the object class, containment procedures, etc etc. The bulk of the article, however, will be inside of the addendum - the interviews, more specifically.

Elevator Pitch: A man under the affect of a seeming "curse". Anyone who verbally confirms any relationship between them and the man dies within the next 24 hours in an unspeakably horrific way, varying from person to person.

Central Narrative: Man of None", a concept I had for an SCP, is a seemingly regular man with a personal love for technology. However, what is strange is the fact anyone who verbally recognizes a relationship between the speaker and the object are killed within 24 hours in an unspeakably painful way. While this may seem as if it's simply for the shock factor of gore and horrific deaths, there's a much darker thing behind it.

+ show block
– hide block

He wants to die, however due to the nature of the SCP Foundation his death would be something which would not be wanted. So, they contain him and give him psychological treatment (of course on a very strict regiment), however it never helps. With plenty of research, the only way which suicide patients are helped is via forming relationships with those who help them. And, any relationship with him causes horrific death. So, he's left alone in the world. All that people will call him is an object. They will not say he's their "friend". Not a "loved one". "Family", "enemy", any of the sort is never heard from them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is a person who has a horrifically frail ego and self-esteem, however wants the best for others. He is absolutely desperate for some form of recognition, approval, or relationship between another human. However, due to the nature of his "curse", he's unable to. This plays to one of the largest human fears of being truly alone. He, at first, tries to isolate himself from other people as to not harm them, however the more he isolates himself the more he becomes desperate to have confirmation in himself and social interaction. And when his greed takes over and he tries to reach out, the people he love die in a horrifically unspeakable way. Watching that is a trauma which most cannot imagine.

Additional Notes: I'm horrific when it comes to formatting first of all, so if I've messed this up please tell me. I'd like criticism on the entire thing really.
